@mbauwens  recently shared a talk on “Alignment for a Major Evolutionary Transition.” https://t.co/1KjgwRbfTZ

It’s a thoughtful contribution, especially in how it explores major evolutionary transitions and multi-level selection to frame AI as a potential catalyst for species-level coordination.

But I think there’s a deeper question beneath it:

What is the new viability variable for the planetary system?

Historically, major transitions succeed when a new regulated variable becomes dominant - i.e. when what determines survival shifts.

Right now, our dominant viability variable is still capital-optimisation with engagement-maximisation and resource capture.

Under those conditions, cooperation-centred AI will struggle to outcompete extractive AI, no matter how elegant the transition mechanics.

The talk focuses primarily on transition mechanics:
– multi-level selection
– cooperation design
– collective intelligence scaling
– population structure

All important.

But system mechanics operate within constraints.

My work has been oriented toward something prior:
Substrate conditions.

Before a system can transition coherently, it must restore:
– ethical constraint (dignity, inclusion, non-instrumentalisation)
– epistemic integrity (feedback that isn’t captured)
– temporal discernment (right-timed action rather than acceleration)

Without these, evolutionary acceleration amplifies the wrong attractor.

If capital accumulation remains the governing viability variable, AI becomes a coherence extractor rather than a coherence amplifier.

So for me the real alignment question isn’t:

“Can we design cooperative AI?”

It is:

Can we shift the planetary viability variable from capital-optimisation to life-coherence?

Transition mechanics matter.
But substrate conditions determine what emerges, grows and survives.

That’s where I believe the deeper work lies.

* Human Energy: Alignment for a Major Evolutionary Transition: The Future of Humanity 

https://t.co/D1460jLQsl via @YouTube 

"How do we align humanity, technology, and the planet as we enter a major evolutionary transition?  

Hosted by Human Energy, the evening wove together evolutionary science, cooperation theory, cognition, and AI through perspectives from Terry Deacon (UC Berkeley), Athena Aktipis (Cooperative Futures Institute), Peter Fenton (Benchmark Capital), and Nichol Bradford (Human + Tech Week).  The panel reframed “alignment” as a human-to-human challenge supported by AI—emphasizing that real progress depends on strengthening cooperation, shared identity, and psychological maturity. They highlighted lessons from major evolutionary transitions: large-scale alignment succeeds when systems reward prosocial behavior, suppress fragmentation, and build reliable channels of communication and meaning.  Speakers pointed to both the opportunities and risks ahead. AI can amplify cooperation and deepen collective intelligence, but only if designed as cooperative infrastructure rather than extractive technology. Our greatest resources—symbolic communication, adaptability, relational intelligence—must be mobilized to overcome institutional lag, misaligned incentives, and attention-driven business models.  As part of Human Energy’s Global Salon Series, this gathering contributes to a growing movement to advance integrative worldviews, evolve the noosphere, and shape a future of coherence and shared flourishing."
